---
title: "Glossary"
---
The codes, symbols and status words used on the pages for readers of this site. Where the 1968 report defines a term itself, its own definition is quoted with the page it is printed on.

## Soils {#soils}

| code | soil | the report's definition | where printed |
| --------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| [RS]{.term title="red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded | Red narrowly-graded crushed volcanic scoria; one of the basic soil types used in the LM SMS. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-3, PDF 28 |
| [PS]{.term title="white crushed pumice, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | white crushed pumice, narrowly graded | White narrowly graded crushed pumice; a basic test soil type used in the LM SMS. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-3, PDF 28 |
| [RSM-a]{.term title="RS mixed with crushed marble, 5 to 7 by weight, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | RS mixed with crushed marble, 5 to 7 by weight, narrowly graded | A narrowly-graded mixture of five parts of RS material and seven parts of crushed marble by weight; one of the basic soil types used in the LM SMS. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-3, PDF 28 |
| [RSM-b]{.term title="RS mixed with crushed marble, 1 to 3 by weight, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | RS mixed with crushed marble, 1 to 3 by weight, narrowly graded | A narrowly-graded mixture of one part of RS material and three parts of crushed marble by weight; one of the basic soil types used in the LM SMS. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-3, PDF 28 |
| [RC2]{.term title="red crushed volcanic scoria, broadly graded" tabindex="0"} | red crushed volcanic scoria, broadly graded | Red broadly-graded "crusher run" andesitic volcanic scoria; one of the basic soil types used in the LM SMS. It was obtained from the same source as the RS material. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-3, PDF 28 |
| [SS]{.term title="white silica sand (Wedron 4040), narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} | white silica sand (Wedron 4040), narrowly graded | White Silica Sand (Wedron 4040-narrowly graded) | AM-68-1 Vol. I, Table 2-3, printed 2-16, PDF 41 |
| [LSM]{.term title="broadly graded scoria (RC2) mixed with air-floated clay" tabindex="0"} | broadly graded scoria (RC2) mixed with air-floated clay | A basic test soil type used in the LM SMS; a mixture of crushed volcanic scoria (RC2) and air-floated clay designed to simulate certain features of the lunar soil as indicated by the Surveyor I photographs. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-2, PDF 27 |

A *narrowly graded* soil has grains of nearly one size; a *broadly graded* one mixes a wide range of sizes. [RSM]{.term title="RS mixed with crushed marble (RSM-a or RSM-b)" tabindex="0"} stands for either mixture of [RS]{.term title="red crushed volcanic scoria, narrowly graded" tabindex="0"} and crushed marble. The report's soil table gives each soil at one or more states, numbered 1 to 12 (the [Soils](../materials/index.qmd) page). In the report's definitions, LM SMS is the study itself: the Lunar Excursion Module Soil Mechanics Study (AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-2, PDF 27).

## Soil states {#states}

A state is a range of relative density ([Dr]{.term title="relative density: 0 at the soil's maximum void ratio (loosest) and 1 at its minimum (densest), from the reference void-ratio limits; a bed packed past the reference densest state reads above 1" tabindex="0"}): 0 at the soil's loosest reference state and 1 at its densest reference state (the maximum and minimum void ratios found by the minimum-maximum density tests); a bed packed past the densest reference state reads above 1.

| state | the report's definition | where printed |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| loose | Loose; describing a soil in a loose state of compaction; a soil for which $0.0 ≤ D_r ≤ 0.3$. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-2, PDF 27 |
| intermediate | Intermediate; describing a soil in an intermediate state of compaction; a soil for which $0.3 ≤ D_r ≤ 0.7$. | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-2, PDF 27 |
| dense | Dense (i.e. describing a soil in a dense state of compaction; a soil for which $0.7 ≤ D_r ≤ 1.0$). | AM-68-1 Vol. I, printed 2-2, PDF 27 |

## Test types {#tests}

| code on this site | test | what is measured |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lpt` | load-penetration test, [LPT]{.term title="load-penetration test: a tool is pushed into a soil bed and the load is recorded against depth" tabindex="0"} | the load on a tool (a cylinder or a footpad) pushed into a soil bed, against how deep it has gone |
| `ds` | direct shear test | the shear stress that makes a soil sample slide along a plane, at a set normal stress, and how much the sample swells or shrinks |
| `dpt` | dynamic penetrometer test, [DPT]{.term title="dynamic penetrometer test: a probe of fixed mass falls from a fixed height into the bed and its peak deceleration is recorded" tabindex="0"} | the peak deceleration of a probe dropped into the bed, [Gp]{.term title="peak deceleration of the dynamic penetrometer, in g: the report's index of the density and uniformity of a bed" tabindex="0"} |
| `dens` | density test | the density a soil reaches with a given compaction, or its loosest and densest states |
| `gs` | grain size analysis | the fraction of the soil, by weight, finer than each sieve size |
| `sonic` | sonic modulus test | the stiffness of a soil sample from the speed of a sound wave through it |
| `tx` | triaxial test | the strength of a soil cylinder under a confining pressure |

## Units {#units}

Values are in SI. The reports use customary units; the value as printed is kept beside each converted one. The conversions use exact factors, shown here rounded to seven significant digits.

| printed unit | SI |
| --- | --- |
| inch (in) | 25.4 mm |
| pound-force (lb, lbf) | 4.448222 N |
| pound per square inch (psi) | 6.894757 kPa |
| pound per square foot (psf) | 47.880259 Pa |
| pound per cubic foot (pcf), as a bulk density | 16.018463 kg/m³ |
| inch per minute (in/min) | 0.423333 mm/s |

## Status words {#status-words}

Each point of data carries one status, which says how it was checked.

| status | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| agreed | the two readings, made separately, matched within their reading bounds |
| resolved | the readings differed, and a further reading of the page settled which was right |
| one-sided-verified | only one reading has the point, and the other reader confirmed it on the page |
| one-sided | only one reading has the point, and the other reader has not confirmed it; a person may or may not have checked it (audited and confirmed say so) |
| pending-review | unsettled; not yet decided |
| audited | the readings agreed, and two student reviewers also confirmed the point on the scan |
| confirmed | the point rested on a rule, a further reading or one reading, and two student reviewers confirmed it on the scan |

The lists of tests and soils also carry a status for each row of the index, built the same way: agreed, normalized (matched once units or spelling were made the same), resolved or resolved-with-notes (settled by a further reading, with a note), rule or convention (settled by a documented rule), provisional (a count to be redone), conflict (the report gives two different values) and one-sided.

A **reading bound** is how precisely a point could be read from the printed figure: a half-width, not a standard deviation, and not the uncertainty of the experiment.

## Missing values {#missing}

A value the data do not have is never shown as a blank or a zero, but as one of these:

| shown as | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| not reported | the report does not give it |
| not yet extracted | the report gives it, but it is not in the data yet |
| unreadable | the scan does not allow a reading |
| conflicting evidence | the report gives two different values |
| not applicable | the quantity has no meaning for this test |

## Kinds of record {#kinds}

| kind | meaning | an independent test? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| single | one physical test on one soil bed | yes |
| averaged-series | a curve the report says is averaged from several tests | no |
| derived-series | a result the authors drew from identified tests, such as a failure envelope from several shear tests | no |
| correlation | a fitted curve drawn without the points behind it | no |
| summary | a number that exists only in the text | no |
| sample | a sample from a soil bin, analyzed for grain size and density | a measurement, not a test on a bed |
| run-table | a printed table of separate runs, one physical test per row (the subscale drag tests; the detail correlation drops of the LM model, one record per soil family) | yes, each run |
